title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Setting (continued from p.541). There is a profinite group 𝔊 (more precisely an extension 𝔊 ⊂ G_{ρ,σ}, with 𝔊′ and the 'hatted' Ŝ′, Ŝ appearing as subgroups). It has distinguished elements ρ and σ, conjugation x ↦ ρ(x) = ρxρ^{-1}, commutators [x,ρ] = xρ(x)^{-1}, and an auxiliary element τ with τστ^{-1}σ^{-1} = −1 (a central sign, as in an SL2-type central extension). Parameters μ ∈ Ẑ^×, with integers ν_i(μ) and signs ε_i(μ) = (−1)^{ν_i}. Σ_{ρ,σ} is the set of 'invariants' (ξ,η,μ) such that ξρ is conjugate to ρ^μ, ησ is conjugate to σ^μ, and ξ and η are linked by the relation from p.541 (ξ = ε_2(μ) η l_1^ν, with ν = (μ−1)/2). (49) defines the canonical map 𝒢*_{ρ,σ} → Σ*_{ρ,σ}, (α,β,μ) ↦ ([α,ρ], ε_2(μ)[β,σ], μ). 𝒢^eff is the inverse image of the 'effective' part Σ^eff. (50) shows the 'special' subset S𝒢^eff (α ∈ Ŝ′, β ∈ Ŝ) is cut out by the two sign conditions δ_σ(β) = 1 and δ_ρ(ατ^{ν_3(μ)}) = 1. (51)–(52): Σ^eff is identified with a group B_{ρ,σ} via u ↦ (ξ,η,μ) = ([u,ρ],[u,σ],χ_B(u)), where χ_B is a character B → Ẑ^×. The projection 𝒢^eff → Σ^eff has the explicit section u ↦ (u, uτ^{ν_2(μ)}, χ_B(u)). Verification: [u,ρ] = ξ. Also ε[uτ^{ν_2},σ] = ε·u(τ^{ν_2}σ(τ^{ν_2})^{-1})σ(u)^{-1} = ε·ε·uσ(u)^{-1} = η, because τ^{ν}σ(τ^{ν})^{-1} = (−1)^{ν}. The page then begins describing the full fibre over (ξ,η,μ). The next page does this: the fibre is the set of translates by the centralizers Z_ρ, Z_σ, rewritten through the normalizers N_ρ, N_σ with sign characters ε_ρ, ε_σ and parity characters δ. This leads to a group M_{ρ,σ}[0] = B ×_δ N_ρ ×_δ N_σ. Purpose: within the 'loop equation' study (sequel to La Longue Marche), to parametrize the solutions (α,β,μ) of the conjugacy/lacet equations governing Galois-type (Teichmüller/GT-like) actions on a profinite group with an order-2 element and an order-3 element (ρ, σ). This reduces them to a group B of 'effective invariants' plus torsors under centralizers/normalizers.
errors: Minor: the transcribed first identity '[u,ρ]=uρ(uρ)^{-1}' should read [u,ρ] = uρ(u)^{-1} (= uρu^{-1}ρ^{-1}). The section computation itself is correct, given the relation τ^ν σ(τ^ν)^{-1} = (−1)^ν, i.e. τστ^{-1}σ^{-1} = −1 central.

That the section respects the third component and the linkage relation defining Σ^eff (μ = χ_B(u), and ξ, η jointly satisfying the l_1^ν relation) is asserted via the identification B ≅ Σ^eff from the previous page, not re-checked here.

ideas.what: Map from solution triples (α,β,μ) to commutator invariants (ξ,η,μ) = ([α,ρ], ε[β,σ], μ); solutions ↔ invariants plus centralizer torsors
ideas.modern_name: Parametrization of (twisted) automorphisms of PSL2/B3-type profinite groups preserving conjugacy classes of torsion elements, à la GT 2- and 3-cycle relations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) for GT; Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, Harbater–Schneps for profinite analysis
ideas.where_published: Unpublished notes (Longue Marche sequel); themes announced in Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Explicit section B_{ρ,σ} → 𝒢^eff, u ↦ (u, uτ^{ν_2(μ)}, χ_B(u)), with sign correction via the central element −1
ideas.modern_name: Splitting of an extension / torsor trivialization

ideas.what: Special subset cut out by parity characters δ_ρ, δ_σ (sign/parity conditions)
ideas.modern_name: Restriction to the kernel of a parity (sign) character

missed.claim: A structured parametrization of solutions of the 'loop equation' (lacet) conditions for an order-2/order-3 pair (ρ,σ) by a group B_{ρ,σ} with a character χ_B, plus centralizer/normalizer torsors with sign characters. This leads to a group M_{ρ,σ}[0] = B ×_δ N_ρ ×_δ N_σ that is a GT-like object predating or independent of Drinfeld's formalism. The general framework, rather than this page's routine computation, could be compared with the Lochak–Schneps/Harbater–Schneps descriptions of \hat{GT}.
missed.quote: On a … une section de 𝒢^eff_{ρ,σ} → Σ^eff_{ρ,σ} … donnée par u ↦ (u, uτ^{ν_2(μ)}, μ=χ_B(u))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Could document Grothendieck's own route to GT-type groups via conjugacy invariants of torsion elements in modular-group completions; of historical interest for the genesis of Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory.

deep.surprise_reason: A technical intermediate step (a section and a sign check) in a long unpublished computation. The surrounding program is historically interesting, but this page itself contains routine group-theoretic bookkeeping.
transcription_corrections: The added phrase near the end reads roughly 'l'un des 𝒢_{ρ,σ}(η,μ)' — likely 𝒢_{ρ,σ}(u,μ), as on the next page.
In (52) the arrow source is 'u' (a crossed-out symbol follows it).
